description: Puts the built-in registration animation on a webinar's registration page: the self-running slides from the benefit to the host to the sign-up, either INSTEAD of the video (mode animation) or BELOW it (mode both). Side effect: it writes on the connected WordPress site. Participants see the animation on their next visit; the host's stored video stays stored, so switching back to the video restores the clip exactly. Needs `session_id` and `webinar_id` from wi_list_webinars. `both` needs a video on the campaign and is refused with code needs_video without one. A campaign can render on several pages: without `page_id` and with own copy the site writes nothing and answers code needs_scope while listing the pages, so name one `page_id` or confirm all of them with `apply_to_all`. A page whose animation the host edited by hand is left alone unless you pass `overwrite_edited` with a page_id, and you should ask before that.

apply_to_all.description: Change every page the campaign renders on. Only after the host agreed to that.

benefits.description: The benefit lines of the first slide, in the host's words.

confirm.description: Only after the site answered code admin_editing: the host agreed to overwrite unsaved changes in wp-admin.

cta_label.description: The label of the sign-up button on the last slide.

headline.description: The headline of the first slide, if the host wants their own.

mode.description: animation replaces the video or image with the animation, both keeps the video and puts the animation below it. Default animation.

overwrite_edited.description: Also change a page whose animation the host edited by hand. Only with page_id and only after asking.

page_id.description: Change only this one page of the campaign.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, as wi_list_webinars returned it. Never invent an id.

name: wi_change_registration_animation
title: Put the registration animation on the page
